raw_response:
*Thinking as this farmer...*

My family has farmed this land in Quzhou for generations. We have about 8 mu of flat, irrigated field on the North China Plain. Everyone around here does the same thing: winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land. That rotation is what this land is suited for, what the equipment rental is set up for, what the grain buyers come to collect. I am not going to experiment.

For wheat, I sow in mid-October after rotary tilling. I use an improved variety — our village co-op recommends Jimai 22 or similar. I apply diammonium phosphate at sowing and urea at jointing. I irrigate four times: before sowing to get good germination, a winter water in December to protect roots from freeze, jointing in April, and grain filling in May. I spray fungicide twice for powdery mildew and one time for aphids.

For maize, I seed directly into wheat stubble right after the June harvest — no tillage, to save time and moisture. I use a hybrid like Zhengdan 958 that the seed shop has always stocked. Summer rains help, but I still irrigate once in July if it is dry. I apply one base compound fertilizer and one topdressing of urea at big flare stage.

I keep one small plot near the house for garlic and vegetables for the family but that is not counted here.
